definitions.explanation: A port or harbor on the coast used for maritime shipping and trade. Refers specifically to ports facing the sea, as distinct from river ports or lake ports.

examples.japanese: {横浜|よこはま}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{海港|かいこう}{都市|とし}だ。
examples.english: Yokohama is a famous seaport city.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}の{貨物船|かもつせん}がその{海港|かいこう}に{入港|にゅうこう}した。
examples.english: A large cargo ship entered the seaport.

examples.japanese: この{海港|かいこう}は{古|ふる}くから{国際|こくさい}{貿易|ぼうえき}の{拠点|きょてん}として{栄|さか}えてきた。
examples.english: This seaport has prospered as a hub of international trade since ancient times.

notes:
A compound of {海|かい} (sea) and {港|こう} (port). Refers specifically to ports on the coast, emphasizing their maritime nature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {海港|かいこう}{都市|とし}: seaport city
- {国際|こくさい}{海港|かいこう}: international seaport
- {海港|かいこう}{施設|しせつ}: harbor facilities

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {港|みなと}: port, harbor — the general everyday word for any port
- {港湾|こうわん}: harbor, port — a more formal/technical term emphasizing the harbor infrastructure
- {空港|くうこう}: airport — uses the same {港|こう} character but for air travel

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {港|みなと} is used much more frequently. {海港|かいこう} appears mainly in written, formal, or technical contexts.
